title: Is It Worth Refinishing Hardwood Floors Before Selling a House in Sammamish?
meta: Refinishing hardwood floors before selling in Sammamish: worth it? Usually yes at $3.99 per sq ft; sometimes a $1.99 recoat does it. Wills Flooring explains.
keywords: refinish hardwood floors before selling house, is it worth refinishing floors before selling, hardwood floor refinishing Sammamish, recoat floors before listing, refinish floors ROI

blocks.lead: Usually yes. In Sammamish, where buyers pay a premium for move-in ready and almost every 1990s to 2010s house has builder oak on the main floor, a natural refinish at $3.99 per sq ft is one of the few pre-sale projects that reliably pays for itself. If the floor is just dull with no bare wood showing, a $1.99 screen and recoat gets most of the effect for half the price.
blocks.detail: Those are Wills Flooring's published rates, all-in with three coats of Bona water-based finish, 500 sq ft minimum. Skip it only if the floors are already good or the house is priced as a project.

blocks.html: Sellers in Klahanie, Trossachs and Pine Lake ask us this every spring, usually after their agent walks through and points at the scratched, orange-toned oak in the entry. The floors are 20 to 30 years old, they have survived two dogs and three kids, and the question is whether $5,000 to $7,000 of refinishing comes back at closing. We cannot promise a dollar return; nobody honestly can. But we can tell you what Sammamish buyers react to, what the work costs to the dollar, and when a cheaper option gets you there.

blocks.text: What Sammamish buyers actually react to

items.title: Builder oak, 20 to 30 years in
items.text: Most plateau homes were finished with 2¼ inch red oak and an oil-based finish that has gone orange. Buyers walking in from a staged new-build in Trossachs read that color as dated before they notice anything else. A natural water-based refinish resets it to a clean, lighter tone.

items.title: Dog scratches and gray traffic lanes
items.text: Big families and big dogs are the Sammamish norm. Worn finish in front of the slider and along the kitchen island photographs as gray. Buyers assume the whole floor needs replacing, and they price that assumption at several times what refinishing costs.

items.title: Move-in ready expectations
items.text: Sammamish buyers are typically relocating tech families who want zero projects before the school year starts. Freshly finished floors let the listing say "refinished hardwoods" and let the agent skip a conversation about credits.

items.title: Open plan means one floor
items.text: Because these main floors flow from entry through kitchen to family room, a partial fix looks patchy. The whole connected area gets refinished at once, which is also why the math below uses the full main floor.

items.title: Screen and recoat
items.text: Light abrasion plus a fresh coat of finish. One day, no dust, no color change. Fixes haze and fine scratches only. Not possible if any bare wood or gray shows.

items.title: Sand and refinish, natural
items.text: Full sand to bare wood, three coats of Bona water-based finish. Removes scratches, gray lanes, orange tone and light pet marks. Matte or satin sheen reads current to buyers.

items.tag: Only if the color is the problem
items.title: Sand, stain and finish
items.text: Adds a stain coat and a day. Worth it when the house is styled dark or very light and the natural oak would clash. Otherwise, save the $2.51 per sq ft.

blocks.note: 500 sq ft minimum. Stairs $55 to $75 per tread, dust containment +$250, appliance moves extra.

blocks.text: The math on a typical plateau main floor

items.d: Klahanie two-story · 1,400 sq ft main floor + 14 stairs
items.text: Natural refinish, stairs refinished to match, family staying in the house so dust containment added.

items.d: Pine Lake rambler · 1,100 sq ft, finish dull but intact

blocks.html: Against those numbers, consider what a buyer does when they see worn floors: they either ask for a credit or knock the offer down, and in our experience they do both at a figure well above the refinishing cost, because they are pricing a replacement they will never actually do. Refinishing does not add a room; it removes an objection. On a Sammamish listing, objections cost more than floors.

blocks.text: When it is not worth it

a.title: Worth it when
items: Floors show gray, scratches or the orange 1990s tone
The house is priced as move-in ready
You have 3 to 5 days when the main floor can be empty
The wood has enough thickness left, which we measure at the estimate

b.title: Not worth it when
items: The finish is intact and only dull: recoat at $1.99 instead
You are selling to a builder or as a teardown lot
The buyer will likely open walls and redo floors anyway
You cannot vacate the main floor before photos; a rushed job shows

blocks.title: Do not stain for the trend:
blocks.text: Sellers sometimes ask for the dark espresso or the very pale Scandinavian look they saw online. On a pre-sale job that is a gamble at $6.50 per sq ft. Natural oak in a matte finish offends nobody and photographs well. Let the buyer pick a color later if they want one.

items.html: 5 to 6 weeks before photos: free in-home estimate. We measure the wood thickness, check whether a recoat is possible, and give a firm written quote.
3 weeks out: main floor cleared. Stage furniture into the garage or a pod. Every hour we spend moving furniture is an hour not sanding.
The job: 3 days for natural on a typical main floor, 4 with stain, 1 for a recoat. Socks after 24 hours, furniture back after 72, rugs after a week.
1 week out: staging and photos. Fully cured refinished floors in natural daylight are what the listing photos are built around.
Paperwork for the buyer: keep our invoice. It shows the date, the Bona finish system and the 1-year workmanship warranty, which transfers value to the buyer in a way a credit never does.

blocks.text: Mistakes that turn a good idea into a bad one

items: Refinishing after the photos are taken. The photos are the listing. Do the floors first.
Doing only the living room because the kitchen has an island. Open plans get refinished as one connected floor or the seam shows in every photo.
Ignoring the 500 sq ft minimum on a small job. A 400 sq ft entry and hall bills at 500 sq ft, so add the dining room and use it.

faq.q: How much does it cost to refinish hardwood floors before selling a house in Sammamish?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring's published rates, a natural refinish is $3.99 per sq ft, so a 1,400 sq ft main floor is $5,586 before stairs. Stairs are $55 to $75 per tread. A screen and recoat, when the finish is intact, is $1.99 per sq ft. There is a 500 sq ft minimum on every job.

faq.q: Will I get my money back from refinishing before I sell?
faq.a: Nobody can promise a specific return, and we will not. What we see in Sammamish is that worn floors trigger buyer credits and lower offers that exceed the refinishing cost, because buyers price a full replacement. Refinishing removes that objection. It is a defensive spend that protects your price more than it raises it.

faq.q: Can I just recoat instead of a full refinish before listing?
faq.a: Yes, if the old finish is still intact everywhere with no bare wood, gray boards or deep scratches. A screen and recoat at $1.99 per sq ft takes one day and restores the sheen. It cannot fix color or worn-through spots. We tell you at the estimate which one your floor needs.

faq.q: How long before listing should I refinish the floors?
faq.a: Book the estimate five to six weeks before photos. The work itself takes about three days for a natural finish on a typical Sammamish main floor, four with stain, and one day for a recoat. Allow three days after the last coat before furniture and a week before rugs, then stage and photograph.

faq.q: Should I stain the floors a trendy color before selling?
faq.a: Usually not. Stain costs $6.50 per sq ft instead of $3.99 and locks in a color the buyer may not want. Natural red oak with a matte water-based finish looks current, photographs well and offends no one. Stain only when the house is styled in a way that natural oak would clash with.

faq.q: Do I have to move out while the floors are refinished?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but the main floor must be empty and unused for three to five days, and water-based finish needs 24 hours before socks and 72 before furniture. Many Sammamish sellers time it for a week away or live upstairs with dust containment added for $250.
